I bought my steam controller and steamlink a few hours ago, and have put about an hour in to messing around with the controller. So far it's very awkward. Mouse cursor movement is very good making this controller sweet for games that traditionally can't be played at all with a gamepad, like RTS. For $60 the controller's price point is in a sweet spot. I consider the controller to be as disposable as any of my other gamepads, though I don't have any buyers remorse so far. I honestly just feel like I need to give it more time.

At home I use a logitech k400 with a razer mamba when I need KBM for my living room entertainment PC. Works pretty well, and the batteries in the keyboard last forever - I get anywhere from 9 months to a year of heavy use out of a set of batteries. The multi-touch trackpad is amazing for when you just want to do some non-game stuff without having to break out the mouse.

Yeah I use a rechargeable Logitech Performance MX laser mouse at home which is fine for like web navigation but it kills my wrist to play even strategy games so an FPS would be right out. I want to sit back and play Convoy or Dunegon of Dredmore or something, theres lots of relatively slow paced indie games that don't require a keyboard but just dont have controller support. I don't mind hunching over my desk to play, say, Pillars of Eternity but it seems unnecessary for something stupid like Shattered Planet.

As for the K400, ugh, I'm using one right now, I hate this fucking thing, lol. The space bar gets stuck (and is partially broken), same thing with the left shift, the keys jam and are weird, the trackpad is fine except every now and then it somehow magically reads my pinky as doing the 'undo' gesture, I don't even fucking know how that is possible. I'll admit the price was right, and the battery usage is quite good, but holy shit, I bought it for where I work and regret it every day, even as I type this. The trackpad, though, IS very good and I normally hate trackpads, I just wish it hadn't somehow gone rogue and learned how to see. That seems... wrong to me.
